indicators.note: hair that is styled has been rearranged by a barber, so these letters are dressed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man sports a neatly trimmed beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wear' looks like 'sport' as in wearing a beard, but it means to wear away.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to scrape or rub away a surface by friction, which is wearing it down.

blocks.note: surface reading: a gloomy or unfriendly way of saying hello
setter's reading: the weather opposite of sunshine is icy pellets falling, and the old salutation names exactly that

explanation.surface: Someone says hello in a grumpy, unfriendly way.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL HAIL is an old ceremonial salute, but read literally it is a forecast with nothing but hail, hardly sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a formal salutation of homage, as in Macbeth, so it is literally a greeting.

blocks.note: first meaning: the narrator of Joel Chandler Harris's Brer Rabbit stories
second meaning: twin of Romulus in the legend of Rome's founding

explanation.surface: A relative who played a part in establishing a town.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Remus tells the Brer Rabbit tales; Remus and Romulus are the legendary twin founders of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The storytelling figure is known as Uncle Remus, and the legendary twin raised by a wolf shared Rome's founding.

clue.text: Dispute being second in field event

indicators.note: one item sits in another, so the abbreviation goes inside the athletics event

blocks.note: throwing a heavy disc is a field event in athletics
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: An argument over who came second in an athletics event.
explanation.definitionFit: To discuss a matter is to argue it out or debate it, so the verb fits a dispute.

blocks.note: first meaning: a weighing instrument
second meaning: the small overlapping bony plates covering a fish's skin

explanation.surface: Someone balances plates of fish, like a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish plates' reads as dishes for serving fish; it is the protective covering on a fish's body.
explanation.definitionFit: A weighing machine is a pair of pans or a balance, and fish skin bears thin protective plates of the same name.

blocks.note: first meaning: shouts of applause
second meaning: the toast said when raising a glass

explanation.surface: A shout of celebration wishing everyone good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts of applause are cheering, and raising a glass with the word is a toast wishing drinkers well.

blocks.note: first meaning: to gaze around in every direction
second meaning: the nursery-rhyme egg is drawn plump and spherical, so he appears circular

explanation.surface: Humpty Dumpty glances around from his wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works as a verb (look about) and as a description: Humpty Dumpty, the egg, does look round.
explanation.definitionFit: To peer about is to survey surroundings, and an egg-shaped character has a circular appearance.

clue.text: Lengthen your stride, if a stair tread is missing

definitions.text: if a stair tread is missing

blocks.note: first meaning: walk faster with longer paces

blocks.clueFragment: if a stair tread is missing
blocks.note: second meaning: read literally, one rung of the staircase has gone

explanation.surface: Advice to take a longer pace where a stair is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as a missing stair; the phrase also literally says one stair is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepping out means walking briskly with longer paces, and a stair tread that has gone is a step out of place.

blocks.note: first meaning: persuade someone to think something
second meaning, whimsically: guide someone into faith, making them a believer

explanation.surface: Persuading someone to take up religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal sense: leading someone into faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Inducing someone to think something is persuading them, and the phrase literally guides a person toward faith.

clue.text: Victoria thumbed by Jack for a lift?

definitions.text: Victoria thumbed by Jack for a lift?

blocks.clueFragment: Victoria thumbed by Jack for a lift?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone called Jack hitchhiking with a woman, or at Victoria station
setter's reading: Little Jack Horner put in his thumb and pulled out a fruit, of which Victoria is a variety

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker named Jack thumbs a lift to or with Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a popular English variety of this fruit; in the nursery rhyme Little Jack Horner put in his thumb and lifted one out of a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria is a well-known cultivar of this stone fruit, the one Jack Horner extracted with his thumb.

blocks.note: surface reading: a romantic gesture of clasping fingers
setter's reading: a hold is a ship's cargo space, and hands are workers, so workers who load cargo

explanation.surface: Two people clasping each other's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' is a noun, the cargo space of a ship; 'hands' are labourers, so these are dockers who load and unload it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dock labourers who load and unload ships' cargo work in the holds, making them hold workers.

clue.text: It may be recommended as a sun resort

definitions.text: It may be recommended as a sun resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, to sort again, so the preceding letters are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A travel agent recommends a sunny holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday spot, but split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange the letters before it; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the Bahamas is a well-known Caribbean beach holiday destination, often recommended for sunshine.

blocks.note: surface reading: land reserved for building or planning
setter's reading: developing photographic film, which needs a room without light

explanation.surface: A plot of land earmarked for building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' suggests property; it is the developing of photographs, done in an unlit room.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographers process light-sensitive film and prints in a sealed room kept free of daylight.

clue.text: Dangerous situation that frightened buccaneer to death

blocks.note: first meaning: a road site with many accidents
second meaning: the pirates' death summons in Treasure Island, which brought on Billy Bones's fatal stroke

explanation.surface: A perilous moment that scared a pirate to death.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's Treasure Island the pirate Billy Bones is handed this mark and dies of a stroke soon after.
explanation.definitionFit: A notorious accident location is called this, and pirates in Stevenson's novel handed one over as a sentence of death.

blocks.note: surface reading: a staircase made of timber
setter's reading: dance steps performed in wooden-soled shoes

explanation.surface: A flight of timber stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' are dance moves, and the footwear is wooden, as in the traditional Lancashire style.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional folk dance is performed in wooden-soled shoes that beat out the rhythm on the floor.

blocks.note: first meaning: merely, simply
second meaning: equitable, right

explanation.surface: A remark that something is the right thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means merely as an adverb and equitable or morally right as an adjective.

clue.text: Emotional state low, with onset of depression

indicators.note: an onset is a beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone feels down as depression sets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for gloom; it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A mood is a temporary frame of mind or feeling, an emotional state.

blocks.note: first meaning: a step taken, as in drastic ..., or a parliamentary bill
second meaning: an old stately courtly dance

explanation.surface: A choice between performing a play or dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A legislative bill or course of action is called a measure, and the word is also an archaic name for a grave courtly dance.

clue.text: Retired permanently on grounds of ill health

definitions.text: Retired permanently on grounds of ill health

blocks.clueFragment: Retired permanently on grounds of ill health
blocks.note: surface reading: someone taking early retirement from work due to sickness
setter's reading: retire means go to bed, so someone confined there for good by illness

explanation.surface: An employee pensioned off early because of sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' is the bedtime sense: gone to bed, and kept there by illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone confined to bed by sickness or infirmity cannot get up, having gone to bed for good.

blocks.note: first meaning: a supply kept back for later
second meaning: to arrange a booking in advance

explanation.surface: A book kept in stock at a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A store held back for later use is a stockpile, and booking a table or seat ahead is the verb sense.

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
something guaranteed is certain

explanation.surface: A removal company promises its delivery time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removal' suggests moving house; it means rubbing something out.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasing is wiping something out, so the noun is the act of deleting or taking away.

blocks.note: surface reading: a training course or repair shop at the BBC headquarters
setter's reading: an artist's workroom, which also names the room programmes are recorded in

explanation.surface: A workshop held at the BBC's London headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcasting House is the BBC's London headquarters; the room where programmes are made shares its name with an artist's workroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsman's workroom has the same name as a room where radio and TV programmes are recorded.

clue.text: They're lawless, a little grasping also at half-time

only half the word survives, the rest is dropped

explanation.surface: Footballers behave unlawfully, grabbing at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: BANDITTI is the old Italian plural of bandit; only the first half of TIME, TI, is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: The old Italianate plural of bandit names outlaws, robbers who live outside the law.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: In billiards and pool, a massé is a difficult stroke made with a near-vertical cue to put heavy spin on the ball.

blocks.note: first meaning: thought about from every side
second meaning: soil dug and flipped by a plough

explanation.surface: A field inspected and then ploughed.
explanation.definitionFit: Considering an idea carefully is mulling it from all sides, and a plough flips soil upside down.

clue.text: Squalid place where many people live, 50 in all

definitions.text: Squalid place where many people live

indicators.note: the number goes in the total, sitting inside it

blocks.note: the sum is the whole amount
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A crowded run-down district housing fifty families in total.
explanation.definitionFit: A slum is an overcrowded, run-down urban area of poor housing.

clue.text: Before this time in the past

blocks.note: an archaic word for before
the present moment

explanation.surface: Something that happened earlier, back in history.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means before the present moment, hence at some earlier point, previously.

clue.text: Strict clergyman has a setback in the diocese

the clergyman's title is placed in the bishop's seat

blocks.note: Rev is the abbreviation for Reverend
a see is a bishop's diocese
